This last .Rmd stage checks wolf ancestry from the Bayesian model results with similar standard methods as in Harmoinen et al. (2021) research paper, where i got my primer panel from. That is PCA, DAPC and NewHybrids.

## Libraries, settings, paths and basic setup

```{r setup}
suppressMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(adegenet)
  library(tidyr)
  library(patchwork)
})

# Settings from YAML header, turns them into usable variables
invisible(list2env(params, envir = environment()))

# Uploaded shared functions
source("Code/R_scripts/asp_functions.R", local = TRUE)
settings_used <- data.frame(setting = c("run_date", names(params)),
                            value = c(format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"),
                                      vapply(params, function(setting_value) paste(setting_value, collapse = ", "), character(1))))

# Basic plot theme, fonts and colours.
plot_font <- "Times New Roman"
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_family = plot_font))
ancestry_class_levels <- c("Wolf-like", "Backcross to wolf", "F1-like", "Backcross to dog", "Dog-like")
ancestry_class_colours <- setNames(c("#467378", "#D9AF6B", "#C98A4E", "#AF6458", "#7E4038"), ancestry_class_levels)

# Paths for genotype and graphics outputs
graphics_dir <- file.path("Results", dataset_name, "Graphics")
genotypes_dir <- file.path("Results", dataset_name, "Genotypes_results")

# Shared function for building accurate settings based folder names
run_names <- build_run_names(input_type, use_anchors, anchor_length, threshold_type, error_rate, min_score_fraction,
                             prior_type, prior_het_share, prior_population, prior_floor, probe_type = probe_type,
                             ancestry_prior_shape = ancestry_prior_shape, phi_hom_structure = phi_hom_structure)# ancestry run
genotype_run_names <- build_run_names(input_type, use_anchors, anchor_length, threshold_type, error_rate, min_score_fraction,
                                      genotype_prior_type, prior_het_share, prior_population, prior_floor, probe_type = probe_type,
                                      ancestry_prior_shape = ancestry_prior_shape, phi_hom_structure = phi_hom_structure) #flat run

# Separate output folder for real population setting
ancestry_out_dir <- file.path(graphics_dir, "STAN_Hierarchical", genotype_run_names$bayes_settings_label, paste0("Ancestry_validation_", reference_source))

# Imported shared data
stan_sample_parameters <- read_tsv(file.path(genotypes_dir, run_names$bayes_run_name, "sample_parameters_hierarchical.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) # wolf ancestry per sample from 05

# All the reference, sample and hybrids animals from .rds in the 08a stage
invisible(list2env(readRDS(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "ancestry_inputs.rds")), envir = environment()))

# NewHybrids and STRUCTURE folders and the keys written in 08a
newhybrids_dir <- file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "NewHybrids")
newhybrids_power_dir <- file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "NewHybrids_power")
structure_dir <- file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "STRUCTURE")
newhybrids_key <- read_tsv(file.path(newhybrids_dir, "newhybrids_key.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, na = character())
power_key <- read_tsv(file.path(newhybrids_power_dir, "newhybrids_power_key.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE, na = character())
n_power_per_class <- 100 # same as in 08a, used for a power plot
```



## PCA of genotypes with simulated reference wolves, dogs and hybrids
Next chunk contains principal component analysis similar as in the mentioned research paper, where they used EIGENSOFT smartpca. Here i use adegent package and dudi.pca() with allele frequencies centred and not scaled. Missing genotypes are set to SNP average. It differentiates with the research paper, here I use simulated reference wolves and dogs from the panel using (freqwolf_all and freqdog columns), each locus is set up independently under HWE, no automatic outlier removal because I only have 24 samples, and I use 33 loci instead of 93.

```{r Ancestry_PCA, fig.width = 6.3, fig.height = 5, out.width = "100%", dpi = 300}
### This part runs the PCA, genotypes are converted to allele freq per animal, missing genotypes are replcaed by the allele mean.

# Number table one row per animal, convertes genotypes into numbers 
allele_table <- tab(all_genind, freq = TRUE, NA.method = "mean")

# Only simulated and Stan  genotypees build the PCA, ref and naive are just projected onto the axis
pca_rows <- !(animal_group %in% c("Reference genotypes", "Naive genotypes"))

# PCA, centered at 0, not divided by sd, stores results from 3 axes
genotype_pca <- dudi.pca(as.data.frame(allele_table[pca_rows, ]), center = TRUE, scale = FALSE, scannf = FALSE, nf = 3)
projected_scores <- suprow(genotype_pca, as.data.frame(allele_table[!pca_rows, ]))$lisup # projected on the axis
pc_scores <- rbind(as.matrix(genotype_pca$li), as.matrix(projected_scores))[rownames(allele_table), ] # back in the order of all_genind
variance_explained <- 100 * genotype_pca$eig / sum(genotype_pca$eig)

# Loci with the largest share of PC2. Firrst cleans up and remove everything after the dot, groups by locus and sgets the share of PC2 in %.
pc2_loci <- data.frame(locus = sub("\\..*$", "", rownames(genotype_pca$c1)), share = 100 * genotype_pca$c1[, 2]^2) %>%
  summarise(pc2_percent = sum(share), .by = locus) %>%
  left_join(data.frame(locus = pca_loci, 
                       wolf_allele1_frequency = colMeans(parent_copies[seq_len(n_reference_wolves), ], na.rm = TRUE) / 2), 
                       by = "locus") %>%
  slice_max(pc2_percent, n = 5)

kable(pc2_loci, digits = c(0, 1, 2), row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("Locus", "Share of PC2 (%)", "Allele 1 frequency in reference wolves"),
      caption = sprintf("Five loci with the largest share of PC2 (%.1f %% of variance)", variance_explained[2]))

# Saving the PCA table
pca_scores <- data.frame(individual = rownames(pc_scores), group = animal_group, PC1 = pc_scores[, 1], PC2 = pc_scores[, 2], PC3 = pc_scores[, 3])
write_tsv(pca_scores, file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "pca_scores.tsv"))

### Method comparison for my three ref, stan and naive genotypes
method_comparison <- pca_scores %>%
  filter(group %in% c("Reference genotypes", "Stan genotypes", "Naive genotypes")) %>%
  transmute(sample = sub(" \\| .*", "", individual), group, PC1) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = PC1) %>%
  mutate(stan_difference = `Stan genotypes` - `Reference genotypes`, naive_difference = `Naive genotypes` - `Reference genotypes`) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(stan_difference)))

write_tsv(method_comparison, file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "pca_method_comparison.tsv"))
kable(method_comparison, digits = 2, col.names = c("Sample", "PC1 reference", "PC1 Stan", "PC1 naive", "Stan - reference", "Naive - reference"), caption = "PC1 of every sample with the three genotype methods, largest Stan difference first")

### Plots with ggplot

# data prep, groups in order for the legend
simulated_levels <- c("Simulated wolf", "Simulated second backcross to wolf", "Simulated backcross to wolf", "Simulated F1",
                      "Simulated backcross to dog", "Simulated second backcross to dog", "Simulated dog")
simulated_short_labels <- c("Wolf", "BC2 wolf", "BC wolf", "F1", "BC dog", "BC2 dog", "Dog")
simulated_colours <- setNames(c("#467378", "#9AA582", "#D9AF6B", "#C98A4E", "#AF6458", "#8B775F", "#7E4038"), simulated_levels)

is_simulated <- animal_group %in% simulated_levels
simulated_factor <- factor(animal_group[is_simulated], levels = simulated_levels)
group_means <- tapply(pc_scores[is_simulated, 1], simulated_factor, mean) # mean of every simulated group

panel_theme <- theme_bw(base_family = plot_font, base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
        plot.title.position = "plot", legend.position = "bottom", plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 8, 8))

simulated_scores <- data.frame(PC1 = pc_scores[is_simulated, 1], PC2 = pc_scores[is_simulated, 2],
                               group = factor(simulated_short_labels[as.integer(simulated_factor)], levels = simulated_short_labels))
short_colours <- setNames(simulated_colours, simulated_short_labels)

# Stan genotypes of the samples with their ancestry class from 05
stan_scores <- pca_scores %>%
  filter(group == "Stan genotypes") %>%
  mutate(sample = sub(" \\| .*", "", individual)) %>%
  left_join(transmute(stan_sample_parameters, sample = barcode, wolf_ancestry, wolf_ancestry_low, wolf_ancestry_high,
                      ancestry_class = case_when(wolf_ancestry >= 0.875 ~ "Wolf-like", wolf_ancestry >= 0.625 ~ "Backcross to wolf", wolf_ancestry >= 0.375 ~ "F1-like", wolf_ancestry >= 0.125 ~ "Backcross to dog", TRUE ~ "Dog-like")), by = "sample")

# candidates that arent wolf like
candidate_scores <- filter(stan_scores, ancestry_class != "Wolf-like")
pc1_label <- sprintf("PC1 (%.1f %% of variance)", variance_explained[1])

## 1. Plot , PC1 against PC2 with ellipses for the simulated groups, samples on top. Created in ggplot (all) so they can later be used with patchwork inside a panel. Tried it first with adegent own functions but it didnt look quite right  

p_pca <- ggplot(simulated_scores, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_ellipse(type = "norm", level = 0.675, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = stan_scores, aes(PC1, PC2), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, size = 1.8, colour = "black",
             fill = ancestry_class_colours[stan_scores$ancestry_class]) +
  geom_text(data = candidate_scores, aes(PC1, PC2, label = sample), inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -1, size = 2.6, family = plot_font) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = short_colours, name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(title = "PCA of simulated groups and samples", x = pc1_label, y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f %% of variance)", variance_explained[2])) +
  panel_theme

## 2. Plot, PC1 only with range of every simulated group as a box, samples as points in the top row, similar structure as before
pc1_rows <- c(simulated_short_labels, "Samples")
p_pc1 <- ggplot(simulated_scores, aes(PC1, factor(group, levels = pc1_rows), fill = group, colour = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.4, outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = stan_scores, aes(PC1, factor("Samples", levels = pc1_rows)), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, size = 1.8, colour = "black", fill = ancestry_class_colours[stan_scores$ancestry_class], position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.15, seed = 1)) +
  geom_text(data = candidate_scores, aes(PC1, factor("Samples", levels = pc1_rows), label = sample), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            vjust = -1.3, size = 2.6, family = plot_font) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = short_colours, guide = "none") + scale_colour_manual(values = short_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "PC1 of every simulated group and the samples", x = pc1_label, y = NULL) +
  panel_theme

## 3. Plot, agreement between my Stan ancestry measruments and PC1. Quick check if different methods describe the structure similary.
ancestry_correlation <- cor(stan_scores$wolf_ancestry, stan_scores$PC1)
p_ancestry <- ggplot(stan_scores, aes(wolf_ancestry, PC1)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = group_means, colour = simulated_colours, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = wolf_ancestry_low, xmax = wolf_ancestry_high), width = 0.15, orientation = "y", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 1.8, colour = "black", fill = ancestry_class_colours[stan_scores$ancestry_class]) +
  geom_text(data = candidate_scores, aes(label = sample), vjust = -1, size = 2.6, family = plot_font) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = max(stan_scores$PC1), hjust = 0, size = 2.8, family = plot_font,
           label = sprintf("Pearson r = %.3f (%d samples)", ancestry_correlation, nrow(stan_scores))) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = dup_axis(breaks = group_means, labels = simulated_short_labels, name = NULL)) +
  labs(title = "Stan wolf ancestry against PC1", x = "Wolf ancestry (05), mean and 95 % interval", y = pc1_label) +
  panel_theme

p_pca
p_pc1
p_ancestry

ggsave(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "pca_adegenet.png"), p_pca, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "pca_adegenet.pdf"), p_pca, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", device = cairo_pdf)
ggsave(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "pca_pc1_only.png"), p_pc1, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "pca_pc1_only.pdf"), p_pc1, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", device = cairo_pdf)
ggsave(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "pca_pc1_against_stan_ancestry.png"), p_ancestry, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "pca_pc1_against_stan_ancestry.pdf"), p_ancestry, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", device = cairo_pdf)
```



## DAPC with the simulated groups as known classes

This chunk runs the DAPC, its trained on simulated wolves and hybrids (2100) and asks to which group each of my samples most likely belongs to. Genotypes are first reduced to PCA components (10) and then DAPC finds best ways to disciminate between those groups. Results are similar to class probabilities of NewHybrids. 

```{r DAPC, fig.width = 6.3, fig.height = 5, out.width = "100%", dpi = 300}
# Number principal components kept, if there are too many it can look better seperated than it actually is
n_dapc_pca <- 10
# All the simulated animals for the training set, group is known
simulated_genind <- all_genind[which(is_simulated)]
pop(simulated_genind) <- simulated_factor
genotype_dapc <- dapc(simulated_genind, n.pca = n_dapc_pca, n.da = length(simulated_levels) - 1)

# This part cheks how many PC components DAPC should keep, before it was hard coded as 10, now its actually cross validated. from 1 to 20 it trains DAPC on a set of simualted animals, and tests on the rest.
simulated_allele_table <- tab(simulated_genind, freq = TRUE, NA.method = "mean") # converts to plain number table
set.seed(simulation_seed)

# cross validation, 30 random splits for each PC count, 10 % of animals for testing
dapc_cross_validation <- xvalDapc(simulated_allele_table, simulated_factor, n.pca = 1:20, n.rep = 30, training.set = 0.9, xval.plot = FALSE)
dapc_cross_validation_table <- data.frame(n_pca = as.integer(names(dapc_cross_validation$`Mean Successful Assignment by Number of PCs of PCA`)), correct_percent = 100 * dapc_cross_validation$`Mean Successful Assignment by Number of PCs of PCA`)

write_tsv(dapc_cross_validation_table, file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "dapc_cross_validation.tsv"))
kable(dapc_cross_validation_table, digits = 1, col.names = c("Principal components kept", "Correct assignment of held-back animals (%)"), caption = sprintf("DAPC cross-validation, best: %s PCs (used: %d)", dapc_cross_validation$`Number of PCs Achieving Highest Mean Success`, n_dapc_pca))

# Share of simulated animals that are recognised as the same group from where they "come from"
kable(data.frame(group = names(summary(genotype_dapc)$assign.per.pop), correct_percent = 100 * summary(genotype_dapc)$assign.per.pop),
      digits = 1, col.names = c("Simulated group", "Assigned to own group (%)"), caption = "DAPC self-assignment of the simulated animals", row.names = FALSE)

# Membership probabilities of my 24 Stan (flat prior) genotypes samples
stan_rows <- which(animal_group == "Stan genotypes")
dapc_samples <- predict(genotype_dapc, newdata = all_genind[stan_rows])
dapc_membership <- data.frame(sample = sub(" \\| .*", "", indNames(all_genind)[stan_rows]),
                              assigned_group = as.character(dapc_samples$assign), # dapc class
                              highest_probability = apply(dapc_samples$posterior, 1, max), #probability of the class
                              round(dapc_samples$posterior, 3), check.names = FALSE)

# Table of seven probability columns per sample
write_tsv(dapc_membership, file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "dapc_sample_membership.tsv"))
kable(arrange(dapc_membership[, c("sample", "assigned_group", "highest_probability")], assigned_group), digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Sample", "DAPC group", "Membership probability"), row.names = FALSE)

# Membership probabilities as stacked barplot
dapc_order <- dapc_membership$sample[order(stan_scores$PC1[match(dapc_membership$sample, stan_scores$sample)])]
dapc_long <- data.frame(sample = rep(dapc_membership$sample, times = length(simulated_levels)),
                        group = rep(simulated_short_labels, each = nrow(dapc_membership)),
                        probability = as.vector(dapc_samples$posterior[, simulated_levels]))

p_dapc <- ggplot(dapc_long, aes(factor(sample, levels = dapc_order), probability, fill = factor(group, levels = simulated_short_labels))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.85, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = short_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  labs(title = "DAPC membership probability of the samples", x = NULL, y = "Membership probability") +
  panel_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6.5))

p_dapc
ggsave(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "dapc_membership.png"), p_dapc, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "dapc_membership.pdf"), p_dapc, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", device = cairo_pdf) 
```

```{r Ancestry_Panel, fig.width = 11.69, fig.height = 8.27, out.width = "100%", dpi = 300}
ancestry_panel <- (p_pca + labs(title = paste0("A   ", p_pca$labels$title))) +
```

## NewHybrids power results

```{r NewHybrids_Power_Results, eval = file.exists(file.path(newhybrids_power_dir, "aa-PofZ.txt")), fig.width = 6.3, fig.height = 5, out.width = "100%", dpi = 300}
# Class each simulated hybrid should get in NewHybrids. Second backcrosses grouped with backcrosses
power_expected_class <- c("Simulated F1" = "F1", "Simulated backcross to wolf" = "BC wolf", "Simulated backcross to dog" = "BC dog",
                          "Simulated second backcross to wolf" = "BC wolf", "Simulated second backcross to dog" = "BC dog")

newhybrids_classes <- c("Wolf", "Dog", "F1", "F2", "BC wolf", "BC dog")
# Reads the results, applies the true class from the key and filters for simulated hybrids
power_results <- read.table(file.path(newhybrids_power_dir, "aa-PofZ.txt"), skip = 1, col.names = c("index", "name", newhybrids_classes), check.names = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(power_key, by = "index") %>%
  filter(flag == "") %>%
  mutate(hybrid_probability = F1 + F2 + `BC wolf` + `BC dog`,
         power_class = factor(simulated_short_labels[match(true_class, simulated_levels)], levels = simulated_short_labels[2:6]))

# Expected probability each animal got the rigth class
power_results$expected_probability <- as.matrix(power_results[, newhybrids_classes])[cbind(seq_len(nrow(power_results)), match(power_expected_class[power_results$true_class], newhybrids_classes))]

# Share of correct class per simulated class
power_summary <- power_results %>%
  summarise(animals = n(), correct_percent = 100 * mean(expected_probability > 0.5), hybrid_percent = 100 * mean(hybrid_probability > 0.7), pure_percent = 100 * mean(pmax(Wolf, Dog) >= 0.5), .by = power_class) %>%
  arrange(power_class)

write_tsv(power_summary, file.path(newhybrids_power_dir, "newhybrids_power_summary.tsv"))
kable(power_summary, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("Simulated class", "Animals", "Correct class (%, > 0.5)", "Recognised as hybrid (%, > 0.7)", "Assigned as pure wolf or dog (%)"), caption = "NewHybrids assignment of simulated hybrids of known class (33 loci, Jeffreys priors)")

# Hybrid probability for evey simulated hybrid in power analysis with 0.7 threshold (from reserach paper)
p_power <- ggplot(power_results, aes(power_class, hybrid_probability, colour = power_class)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.7, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5, position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, seed = 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = short_colours, guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = sprintf("NewHybrids hybrid probability of simulated hybrids (%d per class)", n_power_per_class),
       x = NULL, y = "Hybrid probability (F1 + F2 + BC)") +
  panel_theme

p_power
ggsave(file.path(newhybrids_power_dir, "newhybrids_power.png"), p_power, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## NewHybrids results visualizations

```{r NewHybrids_Results, eval = file.exists(file.path(newhybrids_dir, "aa-PofZ.txt")), fig.width = 6.3, fig.height = 5, out.width = "100%", dpi = 300}
# Names for columns with probabilites from result files
newhybrids_classes <- c("Wolf", "Dog", "F1", "F2", "BC wolf", "BC dog")

# Read results table and attaches the key made  in previous chunk and filters only for my 24 smaples
newhybrids_results <- read.table(file.path(newhybrids_dir, "aa-PofZ.txt"), skip = 1, col.names = c("index", "name", newhybrids_classes), check.names = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(newhybrids_key, by = "index") %>%
  filter(flag == "")

# For each sample it finds the most likely class and assigns the name
newhybrids_results$newhybrids_class <- newhybrids_classes[max.col(newhybrids_results[, newhybrids_classes], ties.method = "first")]

# saves probability of the most likely class, prob of being any hybrid and saves the decision from the Harmoinen assignment rules
newhybrids_results <- newhybrids_results %>%
  mutate(highest_probability = pmax(Wolf, Dog, F1, F2, `BC wolf`, `BC dog`),
         hybrid_probability = F1 + F2 + `BC wolf` + `BC dog`,
         harmoinen_call = case_when(hybrid_probability > 0.7 ~ "Hybrid", 
                                    pmax(Wolf, Dog) >= 0.5 ~ "Pure", 
                                    TRUE ~ "Unassigned"))

# Saves results
write_tsv(newhybrids_results, file.path(newhybrids_dir, "newhybrids_sample_classes.tsv"))
kable(arrange(newhybrids_results[, c("animal", "newhybrids_class", "highest_probability", "hybrid_probability", "harmoinen_call")], desc(hybrid_probability)), digits = 3, col.names = c("Sample", "NewHybrids class", "Probability", "Hybrid probability (F1 + F2 + BC)", "Call (Harmoinen et al. 2021)"))

# Same plot as DAPC
newhybrids_plot_order <- c("Wolf", "BC wolf", "F1", "F2", "BC dog", "Dog")
newhybrids_colours <- setNames(c("#467378", "#D9AF6B", "#C98A4E", "#D7C9BE", "#AF6458", "#7E4038"), newhybrids_plot_order)
newhybrids_long <- newhybrids_results %>%
  select(sample = animal, all_of(newhybrids_classes)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-sample, names_to = "group", values_to = "probability") 

p_newhybrids <- ggplot(newhybrids_long, aes(factor(sample, levels = dapc_order), probability, fill = factor(group, levels = newhybrids_plot_order))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.85, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = newhybrids_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  labs(title = "NewHybrids class probability of the samples", x = NULL, y = "Posterior probability") +
  panel_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6.5))

p_newhybrids
ggsave(file.path(newhybrids_dir, "newhybrids_classes.png"), p_newhybrids, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(newhybrids_dir, "newhybrids_classes.pdf"), p_newhybrids, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", device = cairo_pdf)
```

## STRUCTURE Results
This chunk prepares STRUCTURE results, makes a couple of plots and compares it with my Bayesian ancestry run results.

```{r STRUCTURE_Results, eval = length(list.files(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "STRUCTURE"), pattern = "_f$")) > 0}

#Reads all output files from structure saves full full path fo read lines later
structure_files <- list.files(structure_dir, pattern = "^structure_K2_run[0-9]+_f$", full.names = TRUE)

# Running function once per file, reads the lines, one row per animal, finds labels, % of loci missing, population, q for both cluster and lower and upper limit of the 95 % interval, also and attaches file name
structure_runs <- bind_rows(lapply(structure_files, function(file_name) {
  readLines(file_name, warn = FALSE) %>% 
    grep("\\([0-9]+\\)\\s+[0-9]+\\s+:", ., value = TRUE) %>%
    gsub("[(),:]", " ", .) %>%
    read.table(text = ., col.names = c("number", "label", "missing", "population", paste0("X", 1:6))) %>%
    mutate(run = basename(file_name))
}))

# This part solves the label swtiching from STRUCTURE, it doesn't know which one is wolf just assigns 1 or 0. Based on that is saves the right q and right lower and upper limits.
structure_runs <- structure_runs %>%
  mutate(wolf_is_cluster_1 = mean(X1[startsWith(label, "wolf_")]) > 0.5, .by = run) %>%
  transmute(run, label, structure_q = ifelse(wolf_is_cluster_1, X1, X2),
            structure_low = ifelse(wolf_is_cluster_1, X3, X5), structure_high = ifelse(wolf_is_cluster_1, X4, X6))

# Mean over the runs as in the referenced paper, grouped by label
structure_summary <- structure_runs %>%
  summarise(run_sd = sd(structure_q), runs = n(), structure_q = mean(structure_q), structure_low = mean(structure_low), 
            structure_high = mean(structure_high), .by = label) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(case_when(startsWith(label, "wolf_") ~ "Reference wolves",
                                  startsWith(label, "dog_") ~ "Reference dogs", 
                                  TRUE ~ "Samples"), levels = c("Reference wolves", "Samples", "Reference dogs")))

# Simple ummary table grouped by group (smaples, dogs, wolves)
structure_groups <- summarise(structure_summary, animals = n(), mean_q = mean(structure_q), lowest_q = min(structure_q), highest_q = max(structure_q), .by = group)

kable(structure_groups, digits = 3, col.names = c("Group", "Animals", "Mean wolf q", "Lowest", "Highest"),
      caption = sprintf("STRUCTURE wolf q (K = 2, mean of %d runs)", length(structure_files)))

# COmbines results for 24 samples with my Bayesian ancestry run results
structure_samples <- structure_summary %>%
  inner_join(select(stan_scores, sample, wolf_ancestry), by = c("label" = "sample")) %>%
  select(sample = label, structure_q, structure_low, structure_high, run_sd, wolf_ancestry) %>%
  arrange(structure_q)

write_tsv(structure_samples, file.path(structure_dir, "structure_sample_q.tsv"))

# Summary table for html
structure_sample_table <- structure_samples %>%
  mutate(structure = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f-%.3f)", structure_q, structure_low, structure_high)) %>%
  select(sample, structure, run_sd, wolf_ancestry)

kable(structure_sample_table, digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Sample", "STRUCTURE wolf q (95 % interval)", "SD between runs", "Bayesian wolf ancestry (05)"),
      caption = sprintf("STRUCTURE and Bayesian wolf ancestry, Pearson r = %.3f", cor(structure_samples$structure_q, structure_samples$wolf_ancestry)))

### 1. Plot, same classic stacked bar plot for STRUCTURE, faceted by group
structure_order <- structure_summary$label[order(structure_summary$group, -structure_summary$structure_q)]
structure_long <- bind_rows(transmute(structure_summary, label, group, part = "Wolf", q = structure_q),
                            transmute(structure_summary, label, group, part = "Dog", q = 1 - structure_q))

p_structure_bars <- ggplot(structure_long, aes(factor(label, levels = structure_order), q, fill = factor(part, levels = c("Wolf", "Dog")))) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  facet_grid(~ group, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = short_colours[c("Wolf", "Dog")], name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "STRUCTURE ancestry of reference animals and samples (K = 2)", x = NULL, y = "Ancestry proportion (q)") +
  panel_theme + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), panel.spacing = unit(3, "pt"),
                      strip.background = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
p_structure_bars
ggsave(file.path(structure_dir, "structure_barplot.png"), p_structure_bars, width = 16, height = 8, units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(structure_dir, "structure_barplot.pdf"), p_structure_bars, width = 16, height = 8, units = "cm", device = cairo_pdf)

### 2. Plot , wolf q from Bayes and STRUCTURE runs with error bars
sample_q <- bind_rows(transmute(structure_samples, sample, method = "STRUCTURE (95 % interval)", q = structure_q, low = structure_low, high = structure_high), transmute(stan_scores, sample, method = "Bayesian model (95 % interval)", q = wolf_ancestry, low = wolf_ancestry_low, high = wolf_ancestry_high))

p_structure_samples <- ggplot(sample_q, aes(q, factor(sample, levels = structure_samples$sample), colour = method)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.875), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high), size = 0.15, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), sec.axis = dup_axis(breaks = c(0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.875), labels = c("BC2 dog", "BC dog", "F1", "BC wolf", "BC2 wolf"), name = NULL)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#467378", "#C98A4E"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Wolf ancestry of the samples, STRUCTURE and Bayesian model", x = "Wolf ancestry (q)", y = NULL) +
  panel_theme
p_structure_samples
ggsave(file.path(structure_dir, "structure_sample_q.png"), p_structure_samples, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(structure_dir, "structure_sample_q.pdf"), p_structure_samples, width = 16, height = 12.7, units = "cm", device = cairo_pdf)
```



## Combined ancestry results
This chunk produces a dataframe, side by side result for every sample using all the different methods which makes results easibly comparable. MEthods in question are my measured wolf ancestry from the Bayesian model, PC1, DAPC  and NewHybrids, 

```{r Combined_Ancestry_Results, eval = exists("newhybrids_results"), fig.width = 6.3, fig.height = 8.7, out.width = "100%", dpi = 300}
# Creates combined classed for DAPC, adds probabilites per sample and class and keeps the maximum value
dapc_combined <- dapc_long %>%
  mutate(dapc_class = case_when(group %in% c("Wolf", "BC2 wolf") ~ "Wolf-like",
                                group %in% c("Dog", "BC2 dog") ~ "Dog-like",
                                TRUE ~ group)) %>%
  summarise(dapc_probability = round(sum(probability), 3), .by = c(sample, dapc_class)) %>%
  slice_max(dapc_probability, n = 1, by = sample, with_ties = FALSE)

# Prepares one row per sample with column of different ancestry results, Stan ancestry, PC1, DAPC and NewHybrids ordered by PC1
ancestry_summary <- stan_scores %>%
  select(sample, wolf_ancestry, wolf_ancestry_low, wolf_ancestry_high, ancestry_class, PC1) %>%
  left_join(dapc_combined, by = "sample") %>%
  left_join(transmute(newhybrids_results, sample = animal, newhybrids_class, newhybrids_probability = highest_probability,
                      newhybrids_hybrid_probability = hybrid_probability, harmoinen_call), by = "sample") %>%
  arrange(PC1)
write_tsv(ancestry_summary, file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "ancestry_summary.tsv"))

kable(transmute(ancestry_summary, sample,
                wolf_ancestry = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", wolf_ancestry, wolf_ancestry_low, wolf_ancestry_high),
                ancestry_class,
                PC1 = sprintf("%.2f", PC1),
                dapc = sprintf("%s (%.2f)", dapc_class, dapc_probability),
                newhybrids = sprintf("%s (%.3f)", newhybrids_class, newhybrids_probability),
                harmoinen_call),
      col.names = c("Sample", "Wolf ancestry (95 % interval)", "Bayesian class", "PC1", "DAPC class (probability)",
                    "NewHybrids class (probability)", "Call (Harmoinen et al. 2021)"),
      caption = "Ancestry of every sample with all methods, ordered by PC1")

# One long table with all three methods, sample, class, probability (or ancestry share) and method
bar_methods <- c("A   Bayesian wolf ancestry (mean and 95 % interval)", "B   DAPC membership probability", "C   NewHybrids posterior probability")
bar_data <- bind_rows(transmute(stan_scores, sample, group = "Wolf", probability = wolf_ancestry,
                                low = wolf_ancestry_low, high = wolf_ancestry_high, method = bar_methods[1]),
  transmute(stan_scores, sample, group = "Dog", probability = 1 - wolf_ancestry, method = bar_methods[1]),
  mutate(dapc_long, method = bar_methods[2]),
  mutate(newhybrids_long, method = bar_methods[3])) %>%
  mutate(sample = factor(sample, levels = dapc_order), group = factor(group, levels = append(simulated_short_labels, "F2", after = 4)))

# Stacked bar plots per method ordered and same colours (Bayesian ancestry, DAPC and NewHybrids)
p_ancestry_bars <- ggplot(bar_data, aes(sample, probability, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.85, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), width = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ method, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(short_colours, F2 = "#D7C9BE"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  panel_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 6.5),
                      strip.background = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 11),
                      panel.border = element_blank())

p_ancestry_bars
ggsave(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "ancestry_bar_panel.png"), p_ancestry_bars, width = 16, height = 22, units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(ancestry_out_dir, "ancestry_bar_panel.pdf"), p_ancestry_bars, width = 16, height = 22, units = "cm", device = cairo_pdf)

# Agreement table for replicate samples.
replicate_pairs <- ancestry_summary %>%
  mutate(animal = sub("\\.r1$", "", sample)) %>%
  filter(n() > 1, .by = animal)
kable(select(replicate_pairs, animal, sample, wolf_ancestry, dapc_class, newhybrids_class, harmoinen_call), digits = 2,
      col.names = c("Animal", "Sample", "Wolf ancestry", "DAPC class", "NewHybrids class", "Call"), caption = "Ancestry of replicate samples of the same animal")
```
